title: Jailer 2 Nears ₹100 Crore India Net After ₹125 Crore Worldwide Opening
excerpt: Day 2 estimates take the Rajinikanth sequel to about ₹81.7 crore India net, with Tamil and Telugu versions carrying the run as the Hindi belt softens.
body:
• Jailer 2 added an estimated ₹22 crore India net on Day 2 by evening estimates, taking its domestic net to about ₹81.7 crore and putting the ₹100 crore India milestone within reach on Saturday.
  • Day 1 closed at ₹59.70 crore India net across 16,599 shows — Tamil ₹43.35 crore, Telugu ₹12.50 crore, Hindi ₹3.50 crore — with ₹55 crore overseas for a ₹125.25 crore worldwide opening, the third-biggest ever for a Tamil film.
  • The Hindi version softened on Friday morning, with footfalls down over 45% in morning shows, making the weekend trajectory dependent on the Tamil and Telugu belts.
  • Against a reported ₹300 crore budget, the Nelson Dilipkumar sequel needs a long run, not just a big weekend; Rajinikanth's Coolie had collected ₹108 crore India net by the end of its Day 2.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 held its opening-day momentum into Friday, with tracker estimates putting Day 2 collections at about ₹22 crore India net by the evening, for a two-day domestic total near ₹81.7 crore. The sequel's target for Saturday is now a headline number: ₹100 crore net in India inside three days.

Where the money is coming from

The film's engine is the Tamil version, which contributed ₹43.35 crore of the ₹59.70 crore Day 1 India net, followed by Telugu at ₹12.50 crore. Friday's early tracking kept the same shape — Tamil leading, Telugu second — while the Hindi version was the soft spot, with morning-show footfalls down more than 45% on the opening day and the Hindi belt projected at roughly ₹2 crore for Day 2. Overseas, the film opened with ₹55 crore gross, powered by North America, where its premiere day set a $1.4 million mark, the fourth-biggest for a Kollywood film.

The comparisons that matter

Jailer 2's ₹125.25 crore worldwide opening is the third-biggest for a Tamil film, but the sequel's economics are heavier than the original's: tracker Sacnilk lists a production budget around ₹300 crore. The cautionary comparison is Rajinikanth's own Coolie, which had ₹108 crore India net banked by the end of Day 2 — a mark Jailer 2 will cross a day later. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, the film returns Rajinikanth as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, with Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar and Mithun Chakraborty in an ensemble that also features a much-discussed Hrithik Roshan cameo.

What decides the verdict

Opening weekends for star vehicles are bought with advance bookings; verdicts are earned from Monday. Jailer 2's path is clear: hold Tamil Nadu at near-opening levels through Sunday, let the Telugu version compensate for the Hindi shortfall, and the film is positioned for the ₹1,000 crore worldwide conversation the makers have openly courted. A steep Monday drop, on a ₹300 crore budget, would leave even a ₹125 crore opening looking like an expensive start rather than a triumph. Final Day 2 figures are due from trackers overnight.
